children: (“NKGen” or the “Company”), a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on the development and commercialization of innovative autologous and allogeneic natural killer (“NK”) cell therapeutics, today announced that NKGen Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Paul Y. Song, M.D., will present on the potential of troculeucel, the Company’s lead investigational program, for the treatment of neurodegenerative diseases at Biologics Manufacturing Korea 2026, taking place September 17-18, 2026, in Incheon, South Korea.
Use of Troculeucel (Cryopreserved Enhanced Autologous NK Cell Therapy) for Neurodegenerative Diseases
CAR-T & CAR-NK Therapies Case Studies: Next-Gen Cell Therapy & Preclinical Innovation

Dr. Song’s presentation will discuss the use of troculeucel in neurodegenerative diseases, including troculeucel’s mechanism of action in reducing cerebrospinal fluid (“CSF”) neuroinflammatory and protein biomarkers, clinical experience with troculeucel in patients with Alzheimer’s disease (“AD”), Parkinson’s disease (“PD”), and frontotemporal dementia (“FTD”), and the regulatory landscape in Asia that may help expedite the development and commercialization of troculeucel.
A copy of the presentation will be made available on the Company’s website in the

section once the event has concluded. Previously disclosed scientific data on troculeucel for neurodegenerative diseases can also be accessed in the Scientific Publications section. For the latest updates on the Company’s clinical trials and regulatory announcements, please visit the Company’s

Troculeucel is a novel cell-based, patient specific, ex vivo expanded autologous NK cell immunotherapeutic drug candidate. NKGen is developing troculeucel for the treatment of neurodegenerative disorders and a broad range of cancers. Troculeucel is the International Nonproprietary Name (“INN”) for SNK01 assigned by the World Health Organization (“WHO”). The WHO INN approval of troculeucel establishes a universally recognized nonproprietary drug name for SNK01 and marks a significant step on NKGen’s journey toward bringing this therapy to market.

NKGen is a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on the development and commercialization of innovative autologous and allogeneic NK cell therapeutics. NKGen is headquartered in Santa Ana, California, USA. For more information, please visit www.nkgenbiotech.com.
